title: Anthropic guidance: ownership framing makes Claude Fable 5.2 merge repeated code
summary: Anthropic&\#x27;s prompting guidance for Claude Fable 5.2 states that the model responds closely to who a prompt says owns the code it works on. In the vendor&\#x27;s testing on small coding tasks, when a prompt said nothing about ownership or presented the codebase as someone else&\#x27;s, the model tended to add to the existing structure even when that repeated existing code. Adding the sentence "This codebase is yours: what it&\#x27;s for and how it&\#x27;s built are your call, and you&\#x27;ll keep building on it" led the model to merge repeated code in about half of attempts, versus under a tenth without it. These are Anthropic&\#x27;s own reported results on small coding tasks, not an independently measured benchmark.
